hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are in that familiar pre-big-game limbo: licking wounds from a frustrating Dortmund draw ('Arteta Laments Missed Chance'), fretting over squad depth (where's Martinelli's replacement?), yet sharpening knives for the 'Cheats' with tifo plans and tactical debates about shifting Saka left to unleash the kids. History provides comfort (Henry destroying Barthez, Bergkamp still converting souls), but the present feels like a tightrope walk over the January window.

daily.summary: Arsenal fans moved from raw post-match frustration (4/10) in the early hours to a more anxious, expectation-managing apprehension (6/10) by evening. The constant thread is dominant but profligate performances — 30 shots, one goal — sparking striker panic and tactical nitpicking, while an underlying acceptance persists that the team remains title-caliber if they can just finish. The looming Man City showdown has shifted the mood from angry to nervously anticipatory.

weekly.summary: After riding a wave of euphoric confidence through mid-week — fueled by contract extensions, academy breakthroughs, and table-topping form — Arsenal fan sentiment collapsed dramatically over the weekend. A catastrophic Newcastle draw, Raya's injury scare, and the women's team's managerial crisis triggered a plunge from near-peak optimism (9/10) to structural anxiety (4/10), leaving the fanbase convinced their fragile lead could evaporate at any moment.
